summary: The source contract bounds n by 2^31 - 1, so every legal input contains at most 31 set bits and no honest asymptotic runtime-scaling dimension exists.

workload_bound.source_constraint: The source-fidelity-verified constraint 1 <= n <= 2^31 - 1 limits the positive integer representation to at most 31 set bit positions.

replacement_checks.evidence: Each loop iteration applies n & (n - 1), which clears exactly one set bit, and increments the result once. The loop therefore runs exactly b times with b <= 31, proving O(1) time and O(1) auxiliary space under the bounded source domain.
Black-box real-test execution verifies every existing ordinary check without inspecting its definition, including the integer input and population-count return path.
